competitors.name: CPG brands and grocery retailers
competitors.action: Supermarket News reported an Omnisend survey of 1,075 U.S. consumers found 85% believe brands and retailers often use inflation as an excuse to raise prices more than necessary. The same survey found 67% say higher prices have changed how they feel about brands they once liked, and 56% have stopped buying from them.

competitors.name: Grocery retailers
competitors.action: Supermarket News reported Placer.ai data showing 2026 grocery traffic growth is being driven by lower- and middle-income shoppers, more frequent smaller trips and short in-store visits. Visits under 15 minutes accounted for more than 40% of grocery visits in 2025, up from 37.9% in 2022.

competitors.name: Private-label grocery brands
competitors.action: Supermarket News reported PLMA/Circana data projecting store-brand sales at about $277 billion in 2025, above the 2024 record of $271 billion. Private-label dollar sales were up 4.4% in the first half of 2025 versus 1.1% for national brands, while frozen private-label dollar sales rose 3.8% and units rose 2.1% for the 52 weeks ending June 15.

trends.topic: CPG trust pressure from price and shrinkflation
trends.magnitude: 85% of surveyed consumers said brands and retailers often use inflation to raise prices more than necessary; 65% said groceries are where shrinkflation is most obvious.
trends.context: Premium frozen brands need transparent price/value cues because shoppers are actively reassessing brand trust when prices rise or pack sizes change.

trends.magnitude: Visits under 15 minutes accounted for more than 40% of grocery visits in 2025, up from 37.9% in 2022.
trends.context: Quick-trip behavior makes clear freezer signage, simple claims and fast meal-solution positioning more important for premium frozen pizza discovery.

trends.topic: Private label gaining share in frozen and total grocery
trends.magnitude: Private-label dollar sales rose 4.4% in the first half of 2025 versus 1.1% for national brands; frozen private-label dollar sales rose 3.8% for the 52 weeks ending June 15.
trends.context: Retailer-owned brands are becoming stronger frozen-aisle competitors as shoppers prioritize value but continue to reward perceived quality and innovation.
